$comment: Ceremony coverage per provider (ADR 0082 §7). Checked in rather than
fetched: asking a server which ceremony recipe to use for provider-x tells
that server which provider this user is onboarding, which is precisely the
kind of question the sealed store exists so nobody has to answer
Three independent facts per provider, never a precomputed tier. The tier is
a decision, and recomputing it from the facts is what keeps a stale entry
from pinning a provider to a tier its capabilities no longer match.
`native_registration` means the provider publishes an endpoint that creates
the app or client for us. It covers the registration phase and nothing
else: it cannot make somebody signed in, it cannot install on an org the
user has not named, and it cannot prove the result works.
Every id here must name a provider in
crates/connection-broker/src/catalog.json — enforced by a test, so a
ceremony entry cannot outlive the provider it is for.
Absence is meaningful: a provider with no entry resolves to C3 and gets the
copy-paste instructions it has today. That is the honest default, and never

ceremonies.native_registration_note: GitHub App Manifest flow, already implemented in apps/gateway/src/routes/github_app.rs
ceremonies.note: ADR 0039's backup path: register the App, install it on the org, set the backup target. Registration is C0; the sign-in, org-choice and install steps have no recipe yet, so they resolve to C3 and hand the user the instructions.
Application registration is a dashboard form with no documented endpoint. No recipe yet.
API tokens are minted in the dashboard. No recipe yet.
